note: file_permissions capture, single target. The exact command internal/handlers/filepermissions/capture.go builds. SELinux context is present on RHEL and absent on Ubuntu, which is the divergence a hand-written fixture is least likely to get right.
file_permissions capture of a world-readable file, so the recording covers a mode other than 0000.
file_permissions capture of a missing target: non-zero exit, and the exact stderr the handler reports as ErrCaptureIncomplete.
Service unit-state capture, property-named form. Recorded to pin systemd's own property ORDER, which is not the requested order.

The same read with --value: bare values, no names, in systemd's order. This is the form that stored the two properties under each other's keys for 23 releases. Recorded so the defect is reproducible from a real recording rather than described in prose.
Unknown unit: systemd exits 0 with an empty UnitFileState. The handler must not read that as a transposition.

The deadman time spec Kensa emitted from its first release. at(1) has no sub-minute unit, so this is a parse error on every implementation and creates no job, which is why recording it mutates nothing. Recorded so the exact stderr and exit code are a fact in the tree rather than a claim in a commit message. The corrected form is not recorded here because scheduling a real job would make this manifest a mutation.
Queue listing, for the deadman's post-schedule verification path.
Scheduler detection probe for at(1). Answers differently across the fleet, which is why the deadman defect was invisible on some hosts.
